content.title: Move kind- and Source-based Turn behavior into one turnBehavior table
content.intent: This PR refactors how a Turn picks its prompt mode, tools, and delivery: one turnBehavior table replaces scattered agentInvocationId, declaresResult, and kind checks, and a new check guards it.

chapters.caption: One table now says what each kind of Turn gets
chapters.body: TurnBehavior records a Turn's delivery, prompt mode, answer gating, and tool flags [1]. There are four presets: root, a person in a Thread, an agent in a child, and an Automation run [2]. turnBehavior picks one from the Conversation kind, whether a person sent the input, and the automation flag [3].
asks: Why is automationRun a separate flag instead of a kind?

chapters.caption: The executor computes the behavior once and passes it down
chapters.body: executeAgentRun builds the behavior from the kind, the Source, and declaresResult, and gating reads behavior.gated [1]. assemblePrompt now takes promptMode as an argument instead of working it out from declaresResult and agentInvocationId [2]. Tool wiring reads the same behavior to pass turnTools and to decide on agent tools and finishAutomationRun [3].
asks: Does an Automation run still get Slack formatting rules?

chapters.caption: Agent tools are bound during tool wiring, not in the runner
chapters.body: The runner used to bind spawnAgent and messageAgent up front, keyed on agentInvocationId [1]. Now it only passes the binders through the Run's environment [2]. bindAgentTools binds them after it reads the behavior's agents value, and it keeps the rule that a child that is too deep can still message its parent [3]. The CLI's binder now keys on agents too [4].

decisions.question: bindAgentTools has no direct test at head; should one cover none, children, and the too-deep child?

asks: Can anything else still read durability.spawnAgent?

chapters.caption: A person's Turn in a Thread still gets no agent tools, but by a different route
chapters.body: Before, the conversation worker added the "subagents" disabled feature for a Thread [1]. Now the PERSON_IN_THREAD preset sets agents to "none" [2], so bindAgentTools returns nothing. The integration test just drops its assertion on the disabled feature, and nothing replaces it [3].

decisions.question: No test now checks end to end that a person's Thread Turn has no spawnAgent or messageAgent. Is the preset test enough?

asks: Did the subagents disabled feature also change the prompt's disabled-tools list?

chapters.caption: Tool registries read turnTools flags instead of agentInvocationId
chapters.body: createTools now gates reportBlocked, noReply, and the review-desk lock on turnTools flags [1][2]. Subscription and user-customization tools do the same [3][4]. ToolRuntimeContext replaces agentInvocationId with a required turnTools field, which is why many tests now pass a root Turn's tools.

chapters.caption: Delivery helpers and the person-Source check move into the same module
chapters.body: deliversFinalText and postsRunNotices move from automation-result.ts to kind-behavior.ts with the same bodies [1][2]. isPersonInput replaces two private copies of the same Slack-or-web check, one in state.ts and one in session-stop.ts [3][4].

chapters.caption: Unit tests pin each preset, and an eval covers a reply in an Automation thread
chapters.body: A table test checks every kind and input pair, the task rejection, and isPersonInput [1]. The review-desk test builds a child Turn from turnBehavior [2]. The eval checks that a person's reply in an Automation thread gets a normal answer without finishAutomationRun [3]. Script tests show which forms the new check counts [4].
asks: Is there an integration test for a child Event Turn?

chapters.caption: A non-person Turn on a child now counts as a child agent, even outside an Agent invocation
chapters.body: Any Turn on a child without person input now gets AGENT_IN_CHILD [1][2]. Before, only a Run with agentInvocationId got the child prompt mode [3]. Event Turns run on children through the conversation worker [4]. Inference: a child's Event Turn now gets the child prompt and reportBlocked, and loses the review desk and subscriptions.

decisions.question: Should an Event Turn on a child Conversation get the child-agent prompt and tools, not the conversation ones?

asks: Where does a child's Event Turn reply go now?

chapters.caption: Two cases that used to pass silently now throw
chapters.body: executeAgentRun now throws when a child Run has no Conversation row, and treats a Run with no row as a root [1]. turnBehavior throws when a person's input lands on a task Conversation [2]. Both fail the Turn instead of falling back to root behavior.

decisions.question: Has anyone confirmed that no live path runs a child before its row exists, or sends web or Slack input to a task?

chapters.caption: An architecture check stops new kind branches outside kind-behavior.ts
chapters.body: A new rule uses regexes to count kind, parent-edge, agentInvocationId, declaresResult, and person-Source branches in the runtime source [1]. The baseline checker now takes a rule list and an exclude list [2], and main runs it on the source tree [3]. The baseline records the legacy branches that already exist, so each count can only go down [4].

decisions.question: Is a regex count strong enough to keep new branches out, given that aliased or destructured reads can get past it?

asks: Why does agent/index.ts still have 8 baseline sites?

splits.reason: Mixes the turnBehavior refactor with a new architecture-check rule and its baseline; the guard could land on its own.
